market_mood: Middle East supply risk is back front and center — sea mines hitting tankers near the Strait of Hormuz and a Houthi strike on Aramco's Jazan refinery pushed oil higher — while tech stays under pressure from US chip curbs and fresh governance worries at Nvidia.
self_check: My geopolitics and consumer calls have worked far better than my rate and oil-price calls, and my 'high' confidence calls have been poor, so today I cap confidence at medium and lean on supply-risk second-order effects rather than direct oil-price bets.

picks.reason: Crude rose on the tanker mine strikes and the refinery attack, and OPEC+ still hasn't settled 2027 quotas — a tight-supply backdrop for a pure upstream producer.
Altria publicly responded to speculation about a possible offer for Imperial Brands; acquirers in big debt-funded deals usually see their own shares drift lower while uncertainty lasts.
Higher crude from the Gulf attacks feeds straight into jet fuel costs, and airlines have thin margins; a European carrier already flagged bankruptcy risk, a reminder the sector is fragile.
US natural gas infrastructure gains when global gas supply looks risky.
Midstream volumes and a firmer energy tape benefit from renewed supply tightness.

watchlist_notes.note: Stocks ticked lower into the holiday; a hot 4.3% Q3 GDP revision cuts against rate-cut hopes even as tariff headlines are being shrugged off.
Tech is the weakest sector (-4.9% on the week) with chip-export curbs and AI-credit worries dominating the narrative.
Defensive, staples-heavy Dow is holding up better than the Nasdaq as money rotates out of AI names.
No major company news today beyond generic dividend commentary; macro and tariffs are the swing factors.
Only a Pinterest advertising tie-up mention; no direct catalyst today.
Double negative: S&P flags possible credit downgrade on governance risk, and Nvidia has halted server shipments to four Southeast Asian countries.
Reports it may let Meta's shopping agent back on its store, plus ongoing debate about its $220bn capex plan and negative free cash flow.
Gemini 4 Neon launch and its Anthropic stake are supportive stories, but the stock has lagged over the past year.
Gained on the Amazon AI-agent talks report, though its backing of a $4.5bn CoreWeave loan highlights AI credit risk.
Chatter about Tesla shareholders getting SpaceX exposure and Musk's SpaceX share giveaway is speculative, not a fundamental change.
Its own research sees a $450bn AI debt wave — more underwriting fees, but also more credit risk to watch.
Tanker mine strikes and the Jazan refinery attack lift crude, a tailwind for integrated oil earnings.
Gold drifted lower as strong GDP data revived talk of Fed rate hikes rather than cuts.
A 4.3% GDP revision and firmer inflation readings are unhelpful for long-dated Treasuries.

top_buys.pitch: Pure upstream leverage to a crude price that just got a fresh risk premium.
top_buys.why: Oil rose after mine strikes on ships and the Jazan refinery attack revived supply concerns, and OPEC+ is still arguing over 2027 quotas ahead of Sunday's meeting. ConocoPhillips has no refining drag, so higher crude flows straight to cash flow. Energy has lagged the market recently, so positioning is light.
top_buys.risks: OPEC+ could agree to raise output on Sunday, and geopolitical premiums often deflate within days if no supply is actually lost.
top_buys.watch: The OPEC+ meeting on Sunday and Brent's reaction.

top_buys.pitch: A potential big debt-funded bid for Imperial Brands puts the acquirer under pressure.
top_buys.why: Altria issued a formal response to media speculation about an offer for Imperial Brands. Acquirers in large cross-border deals usually see their shares drift as investors worry about leverage and the dividend. Altria is a high-payout name whose shareholders own it for income, so any threat to the balance sheet matters.
top_buys.risks: Altria could rule out a bid entirely, or investors may cheer the strategic logic and send shares up instead.
top_buys.watch: Any confirmed offer terms or a statement ruling out a deal.

top_buys.pitch: Rising crude means rising jet fuel just as airline credit stress reappears.
top_buys.why: Oil climbed on Gulf attacks, and fuel is one of the biggest line items for airlines. Southwest has limited international pricing power to offset it. The Norse Atlantic bankruptcy warning is a reminder of how little cushion the industry has when costs move.
top_buys.risks: Strong holiday travel demand and a quick oil pullback would flip this idea; airlines also rally hard on any fare-increase news.
top_buys.watch: Jet fuel crack spreads and holiday traffic data over the next week.

top_buys.pitch: US natural gas infrastructure gains when global gas supply looks risky.
top_buys.why: Gulf shipping incidents raise the perceived value of secure, domestically produced US gas feeding LNG export terminals. Williams moves a large share of that gas and earns fee-based income. It is a lower-volatility way to play the same theme as Cheniere.
top_buys.risks: Pipeline names are rate-sensitive, and a hawkish Fed narrative after the strong GDP revision could weigh on them.
top_buys.watch: US natural gas prices and LNG feedgas volumes.

top_buys.pitch: Midstream volumes and a firmer energy tape benefit from renewed supply tightness.
top_buys.why: Renewed Middle East supply risk supports US production economics, and ONEOK earns fees on gathering and processing volumes. Energy has underperformed, leaving valuations undemanding. It is a defensive way to add energy exposure.
top_buys.risks: Midstream names trade with rates and commodity sentiment, both of which can turn quickly.
top_buys.watch: OPEC+ output decision Sunday and US rig counts.

summary.top_pick: ConocoPhillips (COP): Pure upstream leverage to a crude price that just got a fresh risk premium.
summary.watch: Sunday's OPEC+ meeting on 2027 quotas and any further shipping incidents in the Gulf.
